h: Beaches, Cliffs and a Very Long Village Street
p: Combe Martin itself is a character. The village stretches up its narrow valley along a single long main street, lined with cottages, pubs and shops, and it ends at a sheltered sandy cove with rock pools at low tide. It's the kind of beach where little ones can happily spend an afternoon with a bucket and net.

Just outside the village, the Great Hangman rises above the sea and is often described as the highest sea cliff in England. The South West Coast Path climbs right over it, and on a clear day the views across the Bristol Channel to Wales are stunning. It's a stiff walk, so best for older children and keen walkers, but even a short climb out of the village gives you a taste of it.

Between Combe Martin and Ilfracombe, Watermouth Castle is a family theme park in the grounds of a nineteenth-century castle, which makes a good second day for younger kids. In Ilfracombe, you'll find a busy harbour with boat trips in season and Damien Hirst's towering Verity statue standing guard at the harbour entrance. Exmoor National Park is right behind the village too, so moorland drives and ponies aren't far away.

Tips for the park: the site runs up and down the valley, so a lightweight buggy is better than a heavy one. Check the times of the animal talks and dinosaur shows on arrival, and go round with those in mind.
